title: Etale gluing of morphisms of schemes with line modules
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with morphisms $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$, and let $L,M$ be invertible modules on $X,Y$, respectively [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Write $X_i=X\times_SU_i$, $Y_i=Y\times_SU_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $L_i,M_i$ for the pullbacks of $L,M$ to these schemes [def-pc-module-pullback]. For each $i$, let $b_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be a morphism over $U_i$ and let $\mu_i:b_i^*M_i\to L_i$ be a module homomorphism. Assume that on $U_i\times_SU_j$ the base changes of $b_i,b_j$ agree and the base changes of $\mu_i,\mu_j$ agree under the canonical pullback identifications. Use the identity and composition comparisons of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] and [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso] for these identifications. Then there is a unique pair consisting of an $S$-morphism $b:X\to Y$ and a module homomorphism $\mu:b^*M\to L$ whose base changes are the prescribed $b_i,\mu_i$. If every $b_i$ and $\mu_i$ is an isomorphism, then $b$ and $\mu$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 023Q (descent lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), etale case for underlying morphisms; spaces-descent.tex Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), full faithfulness for the module maps.

proof.text: Write $a:X\to S$, $d:Y\to S$, $p_i:X_i\to X$ and $q_i:Y_i\to Y$ for the structure maps and projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], the given covering is fpqc. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], both $\{p_i\}$ and $\{q_i\}$ are fpqc coverings. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $X_i\times_X X_j$ with $X\times_S(U_i\times_SU_j)$, preserving both projections; the analogous identification holds for $Y$. Thus the overlap equalities in the hypothesis are exactly the equalities on the overlaps of these two coverings.

source.place: Tags 023Q and 023T: apply the descent statements to the base-changed covering; supporting Topologies Tags 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc) and 022D (lemma-fpqc), part (3).

proof.text: Set $f_i=q_i\circ b_i:X_i\to Y$. Their composites with the two projections from $X_i\times_X X_j$ agree by the assumed equality of the base-changed $b_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to obtain a unique $b:X\to Y$ with $b\circ p_i=f_i$. The maps $d\circ b$ and $a$ to $S$ agree after each $p_i$, since $b_i$ is over $U_i$; the uniqueness clause of the same node gives $d\circ b=a$. The base change of $b$ to $U_i$ equals $b_i$: both have $Y$-component $f_i$ and the prescribed $U_i$-component, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives equality. The same descent uniqueness proves uniqueness of $b$ as an $S$-morphism.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms: gluing compatible maps, then testing the equation over S by uniqueness.

proof.text: Put $A=b^*M$. It is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], hence quasi-coherent, as is $L$, by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\chi_i:p_i^*A\xrightarrow{\sim}b_i^*M_i$ be the comparison obtained from $b\circ p_i=q_i\circ b_i$ and [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. Set $v_i=\mu_i\circ\chi_i:p_i^*A\to p_i^*L$. On $X_{ij}=X_i\times_X X_j$ with projections $r_1,r_2$, the canonical descent isomorphisms of $A$ and $L$ are the composition comparisons $r_1^*p_i^*\cong(p_ir_1)^*=(p_jr_2)^*\cong r_2^*p_j^*$, and the base change of $\mu_i$ to the overlap is $r_1^*\mu_i$ transported by the comparisons for the commutative square formed by $b_i$, its base change $b_{ij}:X_{ij}\to Y_i\times_Y Y_j$ and the first projections. By [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-associativity], applied to the composable triples $(r_1,p_i,b)$ and $(r_1,b_i,q_i)$ and their $j$-analogues, together with naturality of the comparisons in the module, $r_1^*\chi_i$ followed by these identifications equals the descent isomorphism of $A$ followed by $r_2^*\chi_j$ and the same identifications on the $j$ side. Hence the hypothesis that the two $\mu_i$ agree under the stipulated canonical pullback identifications is equivalent to the two $v_i$ commuting with the canonical descent isomorphisms of $A$ and $L$. Fullness of the equivalence in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], clause (1), therefore gives $\mu:A\to L$ with $p_i^*\mu=v_i$. Faithfulness of that equivalence makes $\mu$ unique. After the comparison $\chi_i$, its base change is the specified $\mu_i$. Together with step 2, this proves uniqueness of the pair.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent, full faithfulness (also Spaces Descent Tag 04W8, same proposition label); pullback invertibility: Modules Tag 01C8 (lemma-pullback-locally-free), rank one.

proof.text: Suppose all $b_i$ are isomorphisms. Their inverses $c_i:Y_i\to X_i$ agree after base change, because a functor preserves inverse equations and the inverse of a fixed isomorphism is unique. Apply the construction of step 2 with $X,Y$ exchanged, using [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] and [def-pc-fibre-product], to obtain an $S$-morphism $c:Y\to X$ with base changes $c_i$. On each $X_i$, $c\circ b$ becomes $c_i\circ b_i=\mathrm{id}$, so uniqueness in representable descent gives $c\circ b=\mathrm{id}_X$. The same argument on the covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$ gives $b\circ c=\mathrm{id}_Y$. Thus $b$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms: glue inverse maps and use uniqueness twice.

proof.text:
Suppose also all $\mu_i$ are isomorphisms. Then every $v_i$ of step 3 is an isomorphism. On a double overlap, invert its compatibility equation to see that the maps $v_i^{-1}:p_i^*L	o p_i^*A$ commute with the canonical descent isomorphisms in the opposite direction. Fullness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], clause (1), gives $
u:L	o A$ pulling back to all $v_i^{-1}$. Both composites $\mu\circ
u$ and $
u\circ\mu$ pull back to identities; faithfulness of the same equivalence gives $\mu\circ
u=\mathrm{id}_L$ and $
u\circ\mu=\mathrm{id}_A$. Hence $\mu$ is an isomorphism. This proves the final clause without assuming invertibility of any local map in the existence argument.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent: fullness for inverse maps and faithfulness for their inverse equations.
